introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Duration: one and three quarter hours.**

Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Consider the table below that illustrates the Acceleration Principle. The capital-output ratio is 2:1. 20 million FCFA worth of machines are due replacement each year. Figures are in millions FCFA, except columns 3 and 8 that are in percentages.

| Year | Output (Y) | % change in output | Existing capital | Required capital | Replacement Investment | Net investment | % change in Net Investment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100 | / | 200 | 200 | 20 | 0 | - |
| 2 | 120 | 20 | 200 | 240 | 20 | 40 | ∞ |
| 3 | 150 | | 240 | | 20 | | |
| 4 | 150 | 0 | 300 | 300 | 20 | 0 | |
| 5 | 120 | | 300 | | 0 | | 0 |
incertitudes: La règle « Answer ANY THREE questions » est exprimée par `regles_choix` (3 sur 5, portée PAPER 3). Aucun total de points n'est imprimé pour la question : `points` de l'exercice est vide, et seuls les points imprimés par sous-question sont repris.

Tableau : le sujet laisse vides les valeurs des années 3 et 5 (production en %, capital requis, investissement net) et la variation de l'investissement net des années 3 et 4. La dernière colonne imprimée vaut 0 en année 5 ; elle impose un investissement net de 0 (et non -60, différence brute entre capital requis et capital existant), ce que le corrigé retient et explique.

Les 8 valeurs manquantes (25, 300, 60, 50, -100, -20, 240, 0) sont calculées et recalculées par script. L'accélérateur vaut 2 (investissement net / variation de la production), égal au rapport capital-production 2:1.
Dans le tableau imprimé, la cellule « % change in output » de l'année 1 contient « / » et celle de l'investissement net « - » ; l'année 2 imprime le symbole ∞ ; recopiés tels quels.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Complete the table above. (8 marks)

(ii) Determine the value of the accelerator in the above table. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Completing the table.**

Relationships used (capital-output ratio = 2, that is capital = $2 \times$ output):

- % change in output $= \dfrac{Y_t - Y_{t-1}}{Y_{t-1}} \times 100$.
- Required capital $= 2 \times Y$.
- Net investment $=$ required capital $-$ existing capital (it cannot be negative here: there is no net investment when the existing capital is more than required).
- % change in net investment $= \dfrac{NI_t - NI_{t-1}}{NI_{t-1}} \times 100$.

**Year 3.**

- % change in output $= \dfrac{150 - 120}{120} \times 100 = 25\%$.
- Required capital $= 2 \times 150 = 300$.
- Net investment $= 300 - 240 = 60$.
- % change in net investment $= \dfrac{60 - 40}{40} \times 100 = 50\%$.

**Year 4.**

- % change in net investment $= \dfrac{0 - 60}{60} \times 100 = -100\%$.

**Year 5.**

- % change in output $= \dfrac{120 - 150}{150} \times 100 = -20\%$.
- Required capital $= 2 \times 120 = 240$.
- Net investment $= 0$: the required capital (240) is below the existing capital (300), so no new machines are needed (the printed last column, a 0% change, is consistent with net investment staying at 0).

**Completed table.**

| Year | Output (Y) | % change in output | Existing capital | Required capital | Replacement Investment | Net investment | % change in Net Investment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100 | / | 200 | 200 | 20 | 0 | - |
| 2 | 120 | 20 | 200 | 240 | 20 | 40 | ∞ |
| 3 | 150 | **25** | 240 | **300** | 20 | **60** | **50** |
| 4 | 150 | 0 | 300 | 300 | 20 | 0 | **-100** |
| 5 | 120 | **-20** | 300 | **240** | 0 | **0** | 0 |

The eight missing values are 25, 300, 60, 50, -100, -20, 240 and 0. Consistency check: existing capital in year 3 is $200 + 40 = 240$, in year 4 it is $240 + 60 = 300$, and in year 5 it stays at $300 + 0 = 300$.

**(ii) Value of the accelerator.**

The accelerator is the ratio of induced net investment to the change in output:

$$
\text{accelerator} = \frac{\text{net investment}}{\Delta Y}
$$

- Year 2: $\dfrac{40}{120 - 100} = \dfrac{40}{20} = 2$.
- Year 3: $\dfrac{60}{150 - 120} = \dfrac{60}{30} = 2$.

**The value of the accelerator is 2**, equal to the capital-output ratio (2:1): every 1 million FCFA increase in output requires 2 million FCFA of additional capital.

questions.enonce_markdown: With the use of years 3 and 4 in the table above, briefly explain the functioning of the accelerator. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The accelerator says that **net investment depends on the rate of change (the growth) of output, not on its level**.

- **Year 3:** output grows by 30 (from 120 to 150, or 25%). Required capital rises from 240 to 300, so firms must add 60 of new capital: net investment rises from 40 to 60, an increase of **50%**. A 25% rise in output produces a 50% rise in investment: investment changes by a larger percentage than output (here by the factor 2).
- **Year 4:** output stays at 150 (growth 0%), a high level but no longer growing. Existing capital (300) is equal to required capital (300), so there is no need for new capital and net investment falls to 0, a **fall of 100%**.
- **Conclusion.** Output has not fallen, yet net investment collapses as soon as growth stops. Changes in output are therefore magnified into larger changes in investment; with the multiplier this helps to explain the booms and slumps of the trade cycle. Only replacement investment (20) remains in year 4.

questions.enonce_markdown:
List any

(i) three limitations of the accelerator principle. (3 marks)

(ii) two factors that can increase the size of the accelerator. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three limitations (any three).**

1. It assumes a **constant capital-output ratio**: in reality technology and methods of production change, so the ratio varies.
2. It assumes that **existing capital is fully used**. If firms have spare capacity, they can raise output without investing, so investment responds less than the accelerator predicts.
3. **Time lags and supply constraints:** ordering and installing capital goods takes time, and the capital goods industry may be unable to supply the extra machines at once.
4. Firms invest according to **expectations**: if they believe that the rise in output is temporary, they will not invest.
5. **Finance** may be unavailable (high interest rates, credit rationing), so firms cannot invest even if they wish to.
6. The principle works well only for **firms that do replace and expand machines in a regular pattern**; it is less applicable to services, or to economies in which machines are imported or output increases through more labour.

**(ii) Two factors that can increase the size of the accelerator (any two).**

1. **A higher capital-output ratio:** more capital-intensive methods of production, or longer-lived and costlier machines, mean that more capital is needed for every extra unit of output.
2. **Full use of existing capacity** and **optimistic expectations**: when there is no spare capacity and firms expect growth to last, every rise in output requires new capital, so the whole of the extra capital requirement is turned into investment.
3. Cheap and easily available credit, and rapid technological change, also encourage a bigger investment response.

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is the value of replacement investment zero in year 5? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
- In year 5 output falls from 150 to 120, so the required capital falls to $2 \times 120 = 240$.
- The existing capital is 300, which is **more than is needed**: there is **surplus capital of $300 - 240 = 60$**.
- Replacement investment is the replacement of worn-out machines (20 per year in this table). Because 60 of capital is surplus, firms do not need to replace the 20 worth of machines that wear out: they simply allow the capital stock to fall towards the required level.
- With no net investment and no replacement, **gross investment is zero** in year 5. (This is why the capital goods industries suffer severely when growth slows down.)
